title: Mixtures and Solutions
objective: After this level you can explain how mixtures and solutions differ.
summary: A mixture mingles two or more kinds of matter in amounts that can vary. A cookie is patchy (heterogeneous); a solution is the same throughout, like salt water, air or brass.

cards.headline: Air is a solution. So is brass.
cards.body: No liquid required. To see how a gas and a metal can both be solutions, start with a chocolate chip cookie.

cards.headline: A cookie is a mixture
cards.body: A mixture is two or more kinds of matter mingled together, in amounts that can vary: more chips, fewer chips, still a cookie. That's the difference from a pure substance, which always has the same makeup. In a cookie you can see the parts, chips here and dough there. Chemists call that heterogeneous: not the same all the way through. Granite and a bottle of Italian dressing are the same kind of mixture.

cards.headline: Solutions: mixed all the way down
cards.body: Stir salt into water and the salt seems to vanish, and every sip is equally salty. That's a homogeneous mixture, the same all the way through, and chemists call it a solution. The substance that gets dissolved (the salt) is the solute. The one doing the dissolving (the water) is the solvent. You can keep adding salt, but only up to a limit.
cards.callout: Solute: what dissolves. Solvent: what does the dissolving.

cards.headline: Solutions don't have to be wet
cards.body: Air is a solution: mostly nitrogen and oxygen, evenly mixed. Brass is a solution too, copper and zinc blended evenly into one solid metal. Maple syrup and gasoline qualify as well. So a solution isn't about being a liquid. It's about being mixed so evenly that every part matches every other part.

mascot.line: Common mix-up: a solution doesn't have to be a liquid. Air and brass count too.

cards.headline: Mixtures: sorted
learned: A mixture's recipe can vary; a pure substance's can't
Solution: the same all the way through
Solutions can be liquid, gas (air) or solid (brass)

questions.prompt: In salt water, which substance is the solute?

options.label: The water
options.rationale: The water does the dissolving, so it is the solvent.

options.label: The glass it is in
options.rationale: The container isn't part of the solution.

options.label: Neither, because salt water is a pure substance
options.rationale: Salt water is a mixture: its saltiness can vary.

questions.explanation: The solute is the substance that gets dissolved: here, the salt.

questions.prompt: Why is a chocolate chip cookie a heterogeneous mixture?

options.label: Its parts are unevenly spread, so it isn't the same throughout
Its ingredients have all dissolved into one another
options.rationale: Then it would be a solution, the same all the way through.

options.label: It always has exactly the same recipe
options.rationale: A fixed makeup describes a pure substance.

options.label: It is made of only one substance

questions.explanation: You can see chips in one spot and dough in another: not the same throughout, so heterogeneous.

questions.prompt: Level 3 sorted matter into solids, liquids and gases. Which of these is a solution that is a solid?

options.label: Salt water
options.rationale: A solution, but a liquid one.

options.label: Granite
options.rationale: Solid, but patchy: a heterogeneous mixture.

questions.explanation: Brass is copper and zinc mixed evenly into one solid metal: a solid solution.
